dedupe_keys.name: scalable digital twin for smart campus facility management price gilbert building georgia tech

description: A December 2025 arXiv study by Thyda Siv that proposes a framework for deploying digital twins in smart campus buildings to support facility operations and maintenance, and demonstrates it on the Price Gilbert Building at the Georgia Institute of Technology. The workflow has three steps: reality capture with terrestrial laser scanning and structured point-cloud processing; an enriched BIM model with architectural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, conveying and sensor systems; and a digital-twin environment that links equipment metadata, maintenance policies and simulated IoT data. In total 509 equipment items were modelled and tagged with OmniClass classifications, and ten interactive dashboards show system performance. Results say the framework enables centralised asset documentation, better system visibility and improved preventive and reactive maintenance. Caveats: most IoT data were simulated because the building had only occupancy sensors, so the prototype shows feasibility, not measured savings. Coverage: one library building. Access: the open arXiv paper; no models or data files are linked. Useful as a worked example of a building digital twin for operations and control studies; related records are not yet linked.
